summary: Explains that modules are shipped as a zipped payload in a wrapper script, and the first debugging step: set ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES=1 and run with -vvv to keep and locate the temporary module file.
questions: How can I keep the module files Ansible copies to the target so I can inspect them?
Why can't I see my module's code directly on the remote host?
How do I find the temporary file name of the module Ansible ran?

answer_card.title: Keep remote module files for debugging
answer_card.answer_md:
Modules are packed into a zip inside a wrapper script. To inspect them:
1. Set `ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES=1` on the control host so the temp files aren't deleted.
2. Run with `-vvv` to print the temporary module file path.

This works for localhost and remote hosts.
